whyImportant: High ROI chapter: Geometry unit usually contributes ~6–10 marks; Triangles is a frequent scorer.
Similarity + BPT unlock multiple case-study/numerical questions (including real-life applications like shadows).
Pythagoras (and its converse) is a classic 3–4 mark target and also supports coordinate geometry & trigonometry later.
examPatterns: 5-mark proof: Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT / Thales) OR Pythagoras Theorem proof.
3-mark numericals: Similarity → CPST ratios → find missing length/height (must show similarity first).
2-mark quick hits: Identify similarity criterion (AA/SAS/SSS), find ratio of corresponding sides, or apply BPT directly.
Case-study style: diagram-based questions where you choose BPT vs Similarity vs Pythagoras by spotting cues.
highROIConcepts: Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT / Thales): DE ∥ BC ⇒ AD/DB = AE/EC.
Similarity criteria: AA / SAS / SSS + correct vertex correspondence.
CPST: ratios of corresponding sides & angles once triangles are proven similar.
Areas of similar triangles: ratio of areas = (ratio of corresponding sides)^2 (used in 3–4 markers).
Pythagoras Theorem + Converse: right-angle detection + length finding.
commonMistakes: Assuming parallel lines or similarity without stating the criterion/theorem.
Wrong vertex correspondence (order of letters) → wrong CPST ratios.
Skipping the final line: 'Hence proved' / theorem name / units (costs easy marks).
Using Pythagoras when the triangle is NOT right-angled (or forgetting converse check).
examTips: For any similarity question: write (i) ∠ = ∠, (ii) ∠ = ∠, (iii) therefore Δ ~ Δ by AA (or SAS/SSS).
Always write the CPST ratio line clearly (this is where examiners award marks).
For proofs: write Given / To Prove / Construction (if any) / Proof steps / Hence proved.
Use units in the final answer and box/underline the result (small habit, real marks).

microExamples.question: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC. Write the proportionality relation.
If ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, write two equal ratios of corresponding sides.
If two triangles are similar and AB/PQ = 2/3, what is the ratio of their areas?
A triangle has sides 6, 8, 10. Is it right-angled?
